title: Fault
description: Doc §3.4: 'Parameterised, idempotent, reversible breakage with a canonical diagnostic path.' One of three reusable content primitives (EnvironmentBlueprint, Fixture, Fault), versioned independently of activities -- a Production Sim activity's spec (§3.3 worked example) references faults by id+version in its `faults:` block, applied after the baseline is confirmed healthy. Phase 2 scope: this schema defines the fault as content; contracts/orchestrator.proto's InjectFault RPC is the execution contract (still unimplemented -- faults exist as data only until T2 lands, see PLAN.md Phase 2 sequencing note).

targets.description: What subsystem(s) this fault breaks, e.g. [k8s.pod-lifecycle], [aws.iam, k8s.imagepull].

symptom_class.description: The observable failure signature a learner sees, e.g. ErrImagePull, CrashLoopBackOff, 5xxSpike.

skills_probed.description: Skill slugs this fault exercises diagnostic ability against -- doc §3.4: 'lets the recommendation engine target a fault, not just an activity.'

canonical_diagnostic_path.description: Ordered list of the expected diagnostic steps -- used for the diagnostic_efficiency process signal (§1.3.2) and to constrain the AI mentor's hints (Phase 4).

expected_fix_class.description: Categories of valid fixes, e.g. [attach_policy, add_irsa_annotation, add_imagepullsecret] -- not a single canonical fix, since production faults usually have >1 valid remediation.

detectability.description: How obvious the symptom is from a first glance at basic health checks -- low means it looks healthy until probed specifically.

mean_time_to_diagnose_minutes.description: Calibration input for L4+ time budgets and Elo; refined from real attempt telemetry once faults are actually executed (Phase 2+).

params_schema.description: JSON-Schema-shaped description of the params map this fault accepts (contracts/orchestrator.proto InjectFaultRequest.params is a plain string map at the wire level; this documents what each key means and its constraints for content authors).

reversible.description: Doc §3.4: faults are parameterised, idempotent, and reversible by design -- false is an explicit escape hatch for a fault whose only real remediation is full redeploy, not an undo.

min_tier.description: Minimum execution tier this fault requires to be applied realistically -- e.g. faults needing Docker-in-Docker or kernel-level fault injection need T2; a K8s manifest misconfiguration can run on T1.

handler_implemented.description: Whether InjectFault has a real Go handler wired for this fault id in orchestrator/internal/faultinjection. Faults apply via direct K8s API calls from the orchestrator process (same clientset Provisioner uses) -- the workspace pod itself has no kubectl/cluster credentials to run an apply script from inside it, confirmed against the real bare-ubuntu image (M1.11 gap). A shell-script-per-fault content field was considered and rejected for this reason; do not reintroduce apply_script without first solving that access gap.
